section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that the perfection of the future revelation through mitzvos depends on the prior drawing down achieved through mitzvos now, especially during the time of the Beis HaMikdash, and notes that additions in Torah and mitzvos during exile serve to complete the service even then.
section.t: And it may be said,
that this—that even the revelation of the mitzvos themselves depends on our actions and service now—
even though in the future there will also be fulfillment of mitzvos,
and moreover, the fulfillment of mitzvos then will be in ultimate perfection
(and consequently,
the drawing down through the mitzvos then will also be in ultimate perfection),
is
because in order for the perfection of the drawing down of mitzvos to be in the future, it requires the precedence of the drawing down of mitzvos as it is now.
[And note the mitzvos of the Patriarchs, which were a preparation for the mitzvos after the Giving of the Torah33.]
And it may be said,
that this matter is also primarily through the service during the time of the Beis HaMikdash.
For during the time of the Beis HaMikdash,
man and the world were on a higher level than during the time of exile,
and therefore34,
in the fulfillment of mitzvos during the time of the Beis HaMikdash
[where the person who performed the mitzvah,
and also the physical object through which the mitzvah was done,
were on a higher level]
there was a perfection resembling the perfection of the fulfillment of mitzvos that will be in the future,
and therefore, that the mitzvos of now are a preparation for the mitzvos of the future is primarily in the mitzvos of the time of the Beis HaMikdash.
[And it may be said that this is also one of the reasons why during the time of exile many matters were added to the mitzvos
(enhancements, customs, etc.),
and also in Torah,
and not only particular matters but also general matters
[for the Mishnah was arranged by Rabbeinu HaKadosh during the time of exile
(except that then there was not the difficulty of exile35),
and all the more so the Baraisa and Gemara, which were arranged during the time of exile],
in order that there should be perfection also in the service of Torah and mitzvos during the time of exile,
and through this,
even through the service during the time of exile, they will come to the true perfection of Torah and mitzvos of the future].

section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section distinguishes between the drawing down and the refinement achieved through mitzvos, explaining that the drawing down now is directly for its future revelation, while the refinement now and its future revelation are two separate matters.
section.t: And behold, the difference between the two aforementioned matters in the fulfillment of mitzvos
(the drawing down through the mitzvah and the refinement accomplished through it)
is also in the connection of the service now with the revelation that will come from it in the future.
For in the matter of the drawing down through mitzvos,
since the perfection of the drawing down is that the drawing down be in revelation,
therefore, the matter of
(the service and)
the drawing down now is that its revelation should be in the future.
And in the matter of the refinement through mitzvos,
since the matter of the service is the refinement of darkness,
meaning that in this service it is felt that there is darkness that needs to be refined,
therefore, the service now and the future revelation that will come through it
(And the spirit of impurity I will remove from the earth36),
are two separate matters.

section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains why the maamar does not bring the interpretation that "Yaakov will take root" refers to the descent into exile, and why the order of the two interpretations is as it is, concluding that the mitzvos in the verse refer to drawing down the root of the soul for future revelation.
section.t: And based on this, it will be understood why in the aforementioned maamar it does not bring the interpretation that "will take root" refers to the descent into exile,
and also the order of the two interpretations in the maamar,
for from the fact that the fulfillment of mitzvos now is called in the verse by the term "taking root,"
the matter of taking root
(sowing)
is in order to bring forth growth,
it is proven
that the matter of the fulfillment of mitzvos in this verse is the drawing down through the mitzvah and not the refinement accomplished through it.
And therefore it does not bring here the interpretation that "will take root" refers to the descent into exile,
for the virtue of the service during the time of exile is in relation to the refinement through the mitzvah,
but not so the drawing down through the mitzvah, which is more in the service during the time of the Beis HaMikdash
(as above, sections 3-4).

And this is also why the interpretation that "Yaakov will take root" refers to the fulfillment of mitzvos now comes after and in continuation of the interpretation that "Yaakov will take root" refers to the revelation of the root of the soul that will be in the future,
for the drawing down through the fulfillment of mitzvos now
(in the verse "Yaakov will take root")
is the drawing down of the root of the soul
(as above, section 1),
and the matter of the drawing down is that it will be in revelation in the future,
they will be born.
